official_measurement_examples: statutory allotment land cannot be disposed of or changed to another use without Secretary of State consent where section 8 applies
statutory status depends on acquisition or appropriation for allotment use rather than current visual use alone
section 8 consent considers adequate alternative provision or why it is unnecessary or not reasonably practicable
disposal includes sale lease appropriation or intended change of use in the published guidance
current Ashfield example shows historic allotment holding can still require section 8 consent before another public use
non-statutory allotment land must not be silently treated as statutory allotment land
Secretary of State allotment consent is distinct from planning permission and open-space disposal procedures
allotment status or consent does not establish private title development capacity or final yield
core_rules: statutory allotment is distinct from non-statutory allotment
section8 consent is not planning permission
planning permission is not section8 consent
current non-use does not automatically extinguish statutory allotment status
disposal includes more than freehold sale
alternative provision criteria must be evidenced
consultation evidence is not consent grant
application for consent is not consent
allotment map is not cadastral title geometry
open-space disposal procedure is distinct from allotment consent
appropriation is distinct from planning permission
historic allotment label must retain legal-status evidence
consent does not calculate development yield
no parcel allotment clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
